title: Majestic Interference!
reviewNotes: All 20 saved images and narration re-reviewed; native images 17 and 19 independently establish the complete seven-piece diagrams after ...Rxd5 and ...Bxd5. Four branches check which pawn promotes safely and both independent wrong-pawn errors. Rd5 obstructs Bf3’s diagonal so a8=Q wins; Bd5 obstructs Rd2’s file so d8=Q wins. The preceding eight-piece Rh5+/Rd5 sacrifice remains outside exact verification, and the two capture diagrams are not joined into an invented line.
transcript: White's brilliant idea is to push D7, now getting only one square away from getting a new [music] queen. But of course, black can just play rook to D2 and stop the promotion like this. But white is not done. He has another pawn that can be pushed to A7 and now also threatens to get a new queen. But again, black can simply play bishop to F3 and now stop both promotions at the same time. It seems like white has no way to defend the pawns and the rook is under attack. If the rook tries to come here, now after king to B6, we're going to start dropping pawns. But white knows that only fools will resign and so he decides to play on with rook to H5 check. This is technically a rook sacrifice that cannot be accepted of course, because otherwise white would be able to promote to a new queen. But black can of course simply sidestep with the king. And finally black thinks that he's out of the woods. But it all comes tumbling down after the incredible [music] and majestic rook to D5. Suddenly black realizes that he's completely lost. This incredible sacrifice that looks like the most outrageous move that we could play in this position, sacrificing the rook to every single piece that black has on the board, is actually the only winning move in the position. Remember, both of the pawns are threatening to promote. The rook is blocking the vision of the bishop and of the rook. And if you capture back with the rook, you're still blocking the bishop. While if you take with the bishop, you are still blocking the rook. And so, it is going to be possible [music] for white to promote to a queen and win the game.
